page: Microsoft Azure D4d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 154 GB local SSD for temporary storage.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1896.79 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1566.0, both falling into the average category. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core score of 3867.66 and Geekbench multi-core score of 3357.0 are classified as weak. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds measured at 29.03 GB/sec and 24.04 GB/sec respectively, which are in the bottom 25% of tested hardware.

This resource configuration is suited for general-purpose workloads that do not demand high memory throughput or intensive multi-threaded processing. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight database operations, though Passmark database operations of 1670.03 and Redis SET operations of 3.88 million operations per second indicate performance constraints under heavy database loads. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of a 154 GB local SSD provides integrated storage value for temporary files and caching, making it a balanced option for entry-level enterprise applications that require dedicated CPU allocation without high-performance compute requirements.

It features 16.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 154 GB local SSD. Benchmarks indicate average single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1566.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1896.79. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth performance are relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3357.0 and large-block read bandwidth of 29.03 GB/sec. This server is suited for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and text processing where high multi-threaded performance is not critical. The integrated local SSD provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring temporary storage.
